text: Sarah lived a hundred and twenty-seven years; these were the years of Sarah's life.
Sarah died at Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan, and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.

versions.text: She died at Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan, and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew names Sarah explicitly as the subject. Naming her here also helps oral reading, since a chapter is often read aloud beginning at verse 2 in a lectionary setting; the pronoun leaves the referent less clear.

text: Then Abraham rose from beside his dead wife and spoke to the Hittites:
"I am a stranger and a sojourner among you. Give me a burial site among you, so that I may bury my dead."
The Hittites answered Abraham:
"Hear us, my lord. You are a prince of God among us. Bury your dead in the finest of our tombs. Not one of us will refuse you his tomb for burying your dead."
Then Abraham rose and bowed to the people of the land, the Hittites,
and he said to them, "If you are willing that I should bury my dead, then hear me and plead for me with Ephron son of Zohar,
that he may sell me the cave of Machpelah, which belongs to him, at the end of his field. Let him sell it to me for the full price, so that I may have it among you as a burial site."
Now Ephron was sitting among the Hittites, and he answered Abraham in the hearing of the Hittites, all who came to the gate of his city:
"No, my lord, hear me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. In the presence of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead."
Abraham bowed before the people of the land
and said to Ephron in their hearing, "If you are willing, then hear me: I will pay the price of the field. Take it from me, so that I may bury my dead there."
Ephron answered Abraham:
"Hear me, my lord. Land worth four hundred shekels of silver—what is that between you and me? Bury your dead."
Abraham agreed to Ephron's terms and weighed out for him the silver he had named in the hearing of the Hittites: four hundred shekels of silver, according to the merchants' weight.
So the field of Ephron at Machpelah, facing Mamre—the field with the cave in it and all the trees within its borders—passed

versions.text: So the field of Ephron at Machpelah, east of Mamre—the field with the cave in it and all the trees within its borders—passed
versions.explanation: The Hebrew לִפְנֵי means "before, facing." Verse 19 already renders the parallel phrase "facing Mamre," so "east of" here is both an interpretive addition and inconsistent within the chapter.

text: into Abraham's possession in the presence of the Hittites, all who came to the gate of his city.
After this Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah, facing Mamre, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan.
So the field and the cave in it passed from the Hittites to Abraham as his own burial ground.

versions.text: So the field and the cave in it were secured to Abraham by the Hittites as a burial site.
versions.explanation: מֵאֵת means "from," indicating the source of the transfer, not the agent. "By the Hittites" wrongly suggests they granted or guaranteed it rather than that Abraham acquired it from them.

versions.text: So the field and the cave in it passed to Abraham from the Hittites as a burial site.
versions.explanation: אֲחֻזַּת־קָבֶר denotes a held possession, not merely a location; "his own burial ground" carries the legal sense of secure ownership. Moving "from the Hittites" next to the verb also smooths the sequence of prepositional phrases for reading aloud, since "to Abraham from the Hittites as a burial site" stacks three phrases in a row.
